docs.title: CertMan
docs.text: CertMan is a desktop application for managing X.509 certificates and related PKI data. It helps users generate and inspect key pairs, certificate signing requests (CSRs), certificates, and certificate revocation lists (CRLs), and organize those records in a database. It also includes tools for certificate profiles, revocation workflows, importing and exporting data, and running selected PKI services.

docs.title: Manage PKI records
docs.text:
CertMan stores and organizes PKI information in a database. A typical workflow is to create or open a database, generate or import a key pair, define a certificate profile, create a CSR, and then issue, import, inspect, export, renew, or revoke certificates as needed. Certificate and CRL profiles let you configure the contents of generated artifacts for different use cases.

The application includes record management for key pairs, requests, certificates, CRLs, users, signers, and related CA and profile information. It can also import data or retrieve data through supported URIs. Available record types and operations can depend on the installed edition.

docs.title: Create keys, requests, certificates, and CRLs
docs.text: The Tools menu provides commands for generating key pairs, making certificate requests, registering users, creating certificate and CRL profiles, issuing certificates, creating CRLs, revoking certificates, and opening CA and profile managers. Supported cryptographic algorithms depend on the application build and license; the source includes RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, SM2, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA paths.

docs.title: Exchange and protect data
docs.text: The Data menu includes import, retrieval from a URI, LDAP publishing, and private-key password tools. Some actions require a licensed edition. The application also supports integration settings for services such as LDAP, KMIP, OCSP, CMP, TSP, REG, and SCEP, depending on edition and configuration.

docs.title: Run PKI services
docs.text: The Service menu contains TSP, OCSP, CA, and ACME service dialogs. These let an operator configure a listener, select the relevant signing or TLS certificates and keys, and start or stop the service. Service controls may be unavailable in the unlicensed edition. The separate Server menu provides additional server tools in editions that include them.

docs.title: Suggested getting-started workflow
docs.text:
1. Install the package for your operating system and launch CertMan.
  2. Use File > New to create a database, or File > Open to open an existing one.
  3. Generate a key pair from Tools > New keypair, or import an existing key and certificate.
  4. Create a certificate profile and make a CSR, or use an existing CA and profile to issue a certificate.
  5. Review the resulting records in the main window, then export or publish them as required.
  6. For a service workflow, configure its certificates, keys, profile, and listener in the appropriate Service dialog before starting it.

docs.title: CertMan: Basic Usage
docs.text:
CertMan is a desktop application for creating and managing X.509 certificates, certificate signing requests (CSRs), certificate revocation lists (CRLs), and key pairs. Certificate and CRL profiles let you create test data with different settings and exercise common PKI workflows. It is especially useful for PKI development and testing.

For the original overview and examples, see the CertMan introduction and the CertMan manual articles.

docs.title: 1. Getting started
docs.text:
1. Install and launch the package for your operating system. Package links and version details are listed in the CertMan update history.
  2. Select File > New to create a database, or File > Open to open an existing database.
  3. When creating a database, choose a location and set its password. Store the password safely; losing it may prevent you from accessing the database.
  4. Check Help > License Information to see the current license and available features. Some functions and algorithms depend on the license.

docs.title: 2. Main records and workflow
docs.text:
The tree on the left side of the main window organizes the records. A typical workflow is:

Key pair → certificate profile → CSR or certificate → issue, review, and export

  • KeyPair: a public and private key managed as a pair.
  • CSR: a signed request containing a subject name and public key.
  • Certificate: a CA-signed record that binds a public key to subject information.
  • CA / Signer: CA information and keys used to issue or sign certificates.
  • Cert Profile / CRL Profile: settings for certificate or CRL fields and extensions.
  • CRL: a list of revoked certificates.

Use the Tools menu or right-click the relevant tree item to create, view, or export records.

docs.title: 3. Create a key pair
docs.text:
1. Select Tools > NewKey, or right-click KeyPair in the tree and select New Key.
  2. Enter a name and select an algorithm. For RSA, set the exponent and key length; for an elliptic-curve algorithm, choose a curve.
  3. Generate the pair and confirm that it appears in the key list.
  4. If needed, select the pair and export its public or private key. Export private keys in an encrypted format and store them in a restricted location.

Available algorithms vary by CertMan version and license. For RSA, ECDSA, and SM2 examples, see Creating asymmetric key pairs.

docs.title: 4. Create a CSR
docs.text:
1. Prepare the key pair that will be used by the request.
  2. Open the certificate request (CSR) creation function from the Tools menu.
  3. Enter the subject DN (for example, country, organization, and common name) and select the key pair.
  4. Configure any required request extensions, then generate the CSR.
  5. Review the subject and public key, then export the CSR if needed.

A CSR is a request, not a certificate. Send it to the issuing CA and then import or register the certificate returned by that CA.

docs.title: 5. Issue a certificate with a CA and profile
docs.text:
To issue a test certificate, prepare an issuing CA and a certificate profile first.

  1. Prepare a key pair and CA certificate for a root or intermediate CA. In a test environment, you can start with a self-signed test root.
  2. Use Tools to create a Cert Profile. Set the certificate type, validity period, default subject information, and required extensions.
  3. Select the subject CSR or open the certificate creation function.
  4. Choose the issuing CA, certificate profile, serial number, and validity period, then issue the certificate.
  5. Inspect the issuer, subject, validity, extensions, and signature.
  6. Export the certificate in the required format, such as PEM or DER.

A self-signed test certificate is not trusted by operating systems or browsers by default. Use it only in a test environment, and check the chain and intended purpose before adding it to any trust configuration.

docs.title: 6. Revoke a certificate and create a CRL
docs.text:
1. Select the certificate and run Revoke or the certificate revocation function.
  2. Choose a revocation reason and confirm the record.
  3. Select the issuing CA and a CRL profile, then generate a CRL.
  4. Review the CRL issuer, update times, and revoked-certificate list before exporting it.

Changing a certificate's revocation status does not automatically update CRLs that were already created or distributed. Generate and distribute a new CRL after changing the revocation list.

docs.title: 7. Import, export, and data handling
docs.text:
• Use the Data menu to review supported import, URI retrieval, and publishing functions.
  • Select a record and use its context menu to view details or export it.
  • Before exporting, check the format (such as PEM or DER) and which data will be included. Encrypt exported private keys and restrict file access.
  • Back up the database and private keys separately, and protect the backups as carefully as the originals.

Menus and supported formats may vary by version and edition.

docs.title: 8. Suggested first exercise
docs.text:
Use a separate test database and test keys rather than production keys while learning the workflow.

  1. Create a test database.
  2. Create a CA key pair and prepare a test root certificate.
  3. Create a user key pair and a certificate profile.
  4. Generate a user CSR and issue a certificate with the test CA.
  5. Inspect the certificate and export it as PEM or DER.
  6. Revoke the user certificate and create a CRL to confirm that it appears in the revoked list.

docs.title: CertMan Linux Installation and Startup Guide
docs.text:
This guide explains how to extract the Linux ZIP package and start CertMan with the included CertMan.sh script.

Version note: The filename CertManV234.zip and screenshots below are from CertMan 2.3.4. Package filenames, folder contents, startup steps, and screens may differ between releases. Check the download and update history for the version you are using.

docs.title: 1. Download the ZIP package
docs.text:
Download CertMan for Linux 64-bit

Open a terminal in the directory where the package was downloaded. The commands below assume the ZIP file is in the current directory.

docs.title: 2. Extract the package
docs.text:
Run the following commands to extract the ZIP file and enter the extracted directory:

unzip -q CertManV234.zip
cd CertManV234

The extracted folder contains items such as bin, lib, plugins, translations, and thirdparty_license, as well as the CertMan.sh startup script. Use ls to confirm that the files were extracted.

docs.title: 3. Start CertMan
docs.text:
From the extracted CertMan directory, run:

./CertMan.sh

The script may prompt for Issuer (cn) and Subject (cn) values in the terminal. Enter the issuer and subject Common Names (CN) for the certificate. The values shown in the screenshot are examples:

Issuer (cn): USERTrust RSA Certification Authority
Subject (cn): Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46

The prompts and behavior may vary by release and configuration. If the script does not start, first confirm that you are in the extracted CertMan directory and that CertMan.sh is present.

docs.title: 4. Prepare a database
docs.text: When CertMan opens, select File > New to create a database or File > Open to open an existing one. Choose a storage location and password, and keep the password and database backup safe. For key-pair, CSR, and certificate workflows, see the CertMan Basic Usage Guide.

docs.title: CertMan Windows Installation Guide
docs.text:
This guide explains how to install CertMan using the Windows 64-bit installer. The screenshots below show the CertMan 2.3.4 Setup Wizard.

Version note: The version and filename shown here are examples. Installer filenames, screens, installation paths, and options may change between releases. Check the download and update history for the version you are installing.

docs.title: 1. Download and start the installer
docs.text:
Download the CertMan Windows 64-bit installer

Double-click the downloaded MSI file to start the Setup Wizard. Confirm the product name and version on the welcome screen, then click Next.

docs.title: 2. Choose the installation folder
docs.text: Review the destination folder. Click Next to use the default location. To install to a different location, click Change..., choose a folder, and then click Next.

docs.title: 3. Start installation
docs.text:
Review the installation settings and click Install to begin. Click Back if you need to change an earlier setting.

If Windows User Account Control (UAC) appears, review the installer prompt and approve it to continue. Administrator approval may be required.

docs.title: 4. Wait for installation to finish
docs.text: Wait while the Setup Wizard installs CertMan. Do not close the wizard during installation.

docs.title: 5. Finish and launch CertMan
docs.text:
When the completion screen appears, click Finish to close the Setup Wizard.

Find CertMan in the Start menu and launch it. On first launch, select File > New to create a database or File > Open to open an existing one. See the CertMan Basic Usage Guide for common workflows.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If the Setup Wizard does not start, confirm that the MSI download is complete and try again.
  • If you see an installation permission error, check whether your Windows account has permission to install applications. Managed computers may require administrator approval.
  • If CertMan does not start after installation, note the error message, Windows version, and installer version.
  • To uninstall CertMan, open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps and select CertMan. Database files are managed separately from the application, so back up any data you need before uninstalling.

docs.title: CertMan Features by License Status
docs.text: CertMan can run with a valid license or as an unlicensed version. This page summarizes the feature differences enforced by the application. Availability can also depend on the product edition, build options, and runtime configuration.

docs.title: Feature comparison
docs.text: Feature Valid license Unlicensed version Key algorithms RSA and the other algorithms enabled by the build, including ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, SM2, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA where supported RSA only for key generation, CSR creation, and applicable key/certificate import or export operations Key pairs, CSRs, certificates, and CRLs Normal creation workflows, subject to edition and build Creation is subject to unlicensed-version count limits. The application reports the applicable limit when it is reached; limits may vary by artifact type or build LDAP publishing Available when the relevant configuration is present Disabled Private-key password operations Set and change private-key passwords Disabled Certificate renewal Available where the relevant workflow is supported Disabled PKI services TSP, OCSP, CA, and ACME service controls can be used when included and configured Service controls are disabled Application log tab Available Disabled Viewing, exporting, and deleting existing records Available, with algorithm restrictions applying to relevant exports General record viewing, deletion, and export remain available; key and certificate operations are limited to RSA where applicable

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• “Valid license” means a license accepted by the running CertMan installation. An expired, invalid, or mismatched license is treated as unlicensed.
  • Other edition and build differences still apply. For example, some service integrations and algorithms depend on product edition, compiled features, and available cryptographic providers.
  • Unlicensed count limits are enforced by the application. This document does not state fixed numbers because limits can vary between builds and artifact categories.
  • The application title identifies the unlicensed version. The Help > License Information dialog displays license status and provides available license actions.

docs.title: Getting a license
docs.text: A free trial license may be requested through the CertMan license registration page. See Help > License Information in the application to request, import, or review a license.

docs.title: ACME Service Manual
docs.text: The ACME Service dialog runs an ACME certificate enrollment service. Configure a certificate profile, CA signing certificate/private key, and at least one supported challenge method before starting the service.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose Service > ACME Service from the main window.

docs.title: Configure the service
docs.text:
1. Enter the ACME listener Port. The initial value is the application's ACME service port.
  2. In Certificate Profile, click Select to choose the profile used for issued certificates. Use View to inspect it.
  3. In CA Certificate and Private Key, click Select to choose the CA signing certificate and its private key. Use View to inspect the certificate.
  4. Choose one or more challenge methods by enabling their sections:
  5. Support HTTP01 Challenge: configure the challenge Host and Port. The initial host is 127.0.0.1 and port is 80.
  6. Support DNS01 Challenge: configure the DNS challenge Host and Port. The initial host is 127.0.0.1 and port is 53.
  7. Support TLS ALPN01 Challenge: configure the challenge Host and Port. The initial host is 127.0.0.1 and port is 443.
  8. For a challenge method, check Fix Server to provide a fixed challenge server endpoint. When enabled, the Host and Port fields are disabled; the configured endpoint is passed to the service.
  9. always challenge valid is enabled by default. Leave it checked to use this behavior, or clear it to disable it.
  10. To enable TLS on the ACME listener, check TLS and select a TLS certificate/private key in the enabled TLS Certificate and Private Key section. Use View to inspect the certificate.
  11. Optionally check Set to default to save these settings for the next time the dialog opens.
  12. Click Start. The Start button turns green when the ACME service starts; runtime messages appear in the log.

The certificate profile and CA certificate/private key are required. Enable the challenge methods that your ACME clients will use. If TLS is enabled for the ACME listener, its TLS certificate and private key must be available. The application reports errors for an empty port, unavailable certificate or key records, unsupported PKCS#11 TLS certificates, or a server that fails to start.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Stop stops the ACME service.
  • Log Clear clears the displayed log.
  • Close closes the dialog.
  • Set to default saves the listener port, TLS setting, selected profile and certificates, challenge settings, and always challenge valid choice. If unchecked when the service starts, the saved default is cleared.

docs.title: CA Manager Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the CA Man dialog, titled CA Management. Open it from Tools > CA Manager (Shift+F11). The dialog lets you browse and manage CA certificates, key pairs, and certificate signing requests (CSRs), or select one of these items when another workflow requests it.

docs.title: Management mode
docs.text: In management mode, use the CA Certificate, Key Pair, and CSR tabs to view or delete database records. Select a row, then click View or Delete. The same actions are available from the table's right-click menu; double-clicking a row opens its details.

docs.title: CA Certificate tab
docs.text: Control / column Purpose Include TSP and OCSP Switch the list to signer certificates used for TSP/OCSP, in addition to the issuer certificate list. Algorithm filter Show Any, RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, SM2, ML-DSA, or SLH-DSA certificates. Num Database certificate record number. Expire Certificate expiration time. Algorithm Certificate signature algorithm. Subject DN Certificate subject distinguished name. View Open certificate details. Delete Ask for confirmation, then delete the selected certificate record.

docs.title: Key Pair tab
docs.text: Control / column Purpose Status filter Show key pairs with NotUsed or Used status. Algorithm filter Filter by Any, RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, SM2, ML-DSA, or SLH-DSA. Num Database key-pair record number. RegTime Key-pair registration time. Algorithm Key-pair algorithm. Name Key-pair name. View Open private-key information for the selected key pair. Delete Ask for confirmation, then delete the selected key-pair record.

docs.title: CSR tab
docs.text:
Control / column Purpose Status filter Show CSRs with NotUsed or Used status. Algorithm filter Filter by Any, RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, SM2, ML-DSA, or SLH-DSA. Num CSR record number. RegTime CSR registration time. Subject DN Subject distinguished name from the request. Name CSR name. View Open CSR details. Delete Ask for confirmation, then delete the selected CSR record.

Changing a filter reloads that tab's list. Table rows cannot be edited directly.

docs.title: Selection mode
docs.text: Other CertMan dialogs use CA Manager as a picker for a CA certificate, key pair, or CSR. In selection mode, only the relevant tab is enabled, management buttons are hidden, and OK is shown. Select a row and click OK, or double-click the row, to return the selected database record number to the calling dialog. Use Close to exit without choosing an item.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The dialog requires an open database.
  • Delete actions ask for confirmation and remove the selected database record. Check dependencies before deleting certificates or key pairs used by other records.
  • The Include TSP and OCSP checkbox affects the certificate list; it is not an algorithm filter.

docs.title: CA Service Manual
docs.text: The CA Service dialog starts a Certificate Authority (CA) service. It uses a certificate profile to process requests and a CA certificate/private key to issue certificates. TLS for the listener is optional.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose Service > CA Service from the main window.

docs.title: Configure the service
docs.text:
1. Enter the listener Port.
  2. In Certificate Profile, click Select to choose the profile used to issue certificates. The selected profile number and name appear in the fields; click View to inspect it.
  3. In CA Server Certificate and Private Key, click Select to choose the CA signing certificate and associated private key. Use View to inspect the certificate.
  4. To enable encrypted transport, check TLS. Select the TLS certificate and private key in the enabled TLS Certificate and Private Key section, and use View to inspect the certificate.
  5. Optionally check Set to default to reuse these settings the next time the dialog opens.
  6. Click Start. The Start button turns green when the CA service is running. Runtime messages appear in the log.

A certificate profile and CA certificate/private key are required. If TLS is enabled, its certificate/private key must also be available. The application reports an error when the port is empty, a selected record or key cannot be loaded, or the service fails to start. TLS certificates backed by PKCS#11 are not supported by this dialog.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Stop stops the CA service.
  • Log Clear clears the displayed log.
  • Close closes the dialog.
  • Set to default saves the port, TLS option, profile number, and CA/TLS certificate numbers. If unchecked when the service starts, the saved default is cleared.

docs.title: Get Data from URI Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the get data from URI dialog. Open it from Data > Get data from URI (Ctrl+Alt+U). The dialog retrieves a certificate or CRL from an HTTP(S) or LDAP location and imports it into CertMan.

docs.title: Retrieve an object from a URI
docs.text:
1. Enter or choose a value in URI Address. HTTP and HTTPS URLs are supported; LDAP URIs can include a search DN, scope, filter, and attribute.
  2. For an LDAP URI, review the Scope, Type, and Filter search conditions as needed.
  3. Alternatively, select Use LDAP Host and enter the host, port, and DN, then set the LDAP Type and Filter.
  4. Click Get to retrieve and import the object. Click Close to exit.

CertMan recognizes the returned data as a certificate or CRL and imports it into the corresponding imported list. Successful non-manual URI addresses are saved in the recent URI list.

docs.title: URI Address mode
docs.text:
Control Purpose URI Address Editable address/history field. HTTP and HTTPS are fetched over HTTP; LDAP addresses are queried using the LDAP search parameters. URL= and URI= prefixes are accepted and removed before retrieval. Clear Used URI Clear the locally stored recent URI history. Use LDAP Host Switch from URI mode to a form where host, port, and DN are entered separately.

The URI history is stored in application settings, not in the current database. The most recent successful URI is placed at the top. Manually entered LDAP host requests are not added to that history.

docs.title: LDAP Host mode and search conditions
docs.text:
Field Purpose Host LDAP server hostname or IP address. Defaults to 127.0.0.1. Port LDAP port. Defaults to 389 if left blank. DN Base distinguished name for the LDAP request. Required in this mode. Scope LDAP URI search scope. The current UI offers BASE. Type LDAP certificate/CRL attribute: caCertificate, signCertificate, userCertificate, certificateRevocationList, or authorityRevocationList. Filter LDAP search filter. Defaults to (objectclass=*).

LDAP access uses an anonymous bind in this dialog. In manual Use LDAP Host mode, host and DN are required; the filter and selected attribute are used for the search. The default scope is BASE.

docs.title: Imported records
docs.text:
• Certificates are stored in the imported certificate list. LDAP caCertificate marks the imported certificate as a CA certificate.
  • CRLs are stored in the imported CRL list. CertMan retains CRL update dates, signature algorithm, and distribution point information when available.
  • Failed network, LDAP, or object parsing operations display a retrieval error and do not report success.

docs.title: Related implementation
docs.text: This guide is based on images/get_uri_dlg.png, src/CertMan/get_uri_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/get_uri_dlg.h, src/CertMan/get_uri_dlg.cpp, and the Data > Get data from URI action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: Import Data Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Import data dialog. Open it from Data > Import data (Ctrl+Alt+I). A database connection is required.

docs.title: Import data
docs.text:
1. Select a Data Type.
  2. Enter a Name when importing a private key, CSR, or PFX-related key pair.
  3. For an encrypted private key or PFX, enter its Password.
  4. Keep Use File selected and choose a file with Find, or clear it and paste data into the value editor.
  5. When pasting, choose Value Type (Hex or Base64) and enter the encoded data.
  6. Optionally select To PKCS11 or To KMS when importing a private key, or To KMS for a certificate when supported.
  7. Click OK to import, or Cancel to close.

On success, CertMan adds the imported object to the relevant list and reports Import was successful. The Name field is enabled for key, CSR, and PFX imports, but the source does not require a non-empty name.

docs.title: Data types
docs.text:
Data Type Purpose and result PrivateKey Import an unencrypted private key and create a key-pair record with NotUsed status. Encrypted PrivateKey Decrypt with Password, then import the private key as a key pair. Request(CSR) Parse a CSR and add it to the Request list using the entered name. Certificate Parse and add a certificate to the imported certificate list. CRL Parse and add a CRL to the imported CRL list. PFX Decode a PKCS#12/PFX bundle using Password, then import its certificate and private key. The key pair is marked Used.

The password field is enabled for Encrypted PrivateKey and PFX. The name field is disabled for Certificate and CRL.

docs.title: Source selection and value format
docs.text:
Control Purpose Use File Read data from a selected file. This is selected by default. Find Select an input file. The file filter is adjusted for the chosen data type. Value Type Select Hex or Base64 for pasted input. Value editor Paste the encoded object when Use File is cleared. The adjacent length field shows the calculated data length.

CertMan also accepts a file dragged onto the dialog. With Use File enabled, the dropped path fills the file field; with it disabled, file bytes are decoded into the selected text format in the editor.

docs.title: Key storage options
docs.text:
• To PKCS11 is available only for private-key imports and when the PKCS#11 provider is configured and loaded. The import implementation supports RSA, ECDSA, and DSA for PKCS#11 storage.
  • To KMS is shown in Pro. It can store supported private keys or certificates through the configured KMIP/KMS service.
  • Importing a CSR or CRL to KMS is not supported by this dialog. The dialog reports this if To KMS is selected for either type.
  • In the unlicensed version, only RSA private keys can be imported.
  • When CertMan private-key encryption is enabled, imported internal private keys are encrypted before they are saved.

docs.title: Related implementation
docs.text: This guide is based on images/import_dlg.png, src/CertMan/import_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/import_dlg.h, src/CertMan/import_dlg.cpp, and the Data > Import data action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: License Information Manual
docs.text: The License Information dialog displays the current CertMan license and provides controls to request, load, update, or remove license information.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose License Information from the main window.

docs.title: Review license details
docs.text: On the Current License tab, review the license Email, Issued Date, and Expire Date. The Message tab displays the license-related notice. Select Do stop showing this message for the time being to suppress that notice temporarily.

docs.title: Load or request a license
docs.text:
1. In Request License, enter the account Email and License Key.
  2. Click Get to retrieve and validate the license. If you already have a license file, check Use License File; the button changes to Find, which opens a file picker.
  3. To request a license, click License Request to open the license registration page in a browser. For a free license, enter an email address and click Free License, then confirm the request.
  4. After a successful license change, the dialog offers to restart the application so the change can take effect.

License files are validated before being applied. The online retrieval or free-license request requires the corresponding license service to be supported by the application build.

docs.title: Update or remove license information
docs.text:
• Click Update License to renew the current license, when one is installed. The application reports an error if no license is present or the update cannot be completed.
  • Click Remove to remove invalid saved license information after confirming the prompt.
  • Click Close to close the dialog.

docs.title: CertMan Menu Manual
docs.text: The screenshot shows File, View, Tools, Data, Service, and Help. The Server menu is added in the Pro edition, so it does not appear in this screenshot. Menu availability also depends on the active license. Toolbar visibility can be customized from View.

docs.title: File
docs.text: Menu item Shortcut Description New Ctrl+N Create a new database. Open... Ctrl+O Open an existing database. Remote Database Ctrl+R Connect to a remote database. Logout Ctrl+T Disconnect from the current database. Recent Files — Reopen a recently used database. Up to ten entries are maintained. Quit Ctrl+Q Exit CertMan.

docs.title: View
docs.text:
The View menu is available when a license is active. Its submenus contain checkable items for showing or hiding individual toolbar buttons:

  • File ToolBar: New, Open, Remote Database, and Logout.
  • Tool ToolBar: key generation, request and user creation, certificate and CRL profile creation, certificate/CRL creation, revocation, and the CA/Profile managers. Pro editions also include Make Config and Register Signer.
  • Data ToolBar: Import Data, Get data from URI, Publish to LDAP, Set Passwd, and Change Passwd. Pro editions also include TSP Client.
  • Server ToolBar (Pro): OCSP, TSP, CMP, REG, CC, and KMS server controls.
  • Service ToolBar: TSP, OCSP, CA, and ACME service controls.
  • Help ToolBar: Settings, Clear Log, Log, and About CertMan. Pro editions also include Server Status.
  • Set Default: restore the default toolbar visibility settings. The application may ask to restart to apply toolbar changes.

These controls affect toolbar visibility; the corresponding commands remain available from their main menus.

docs.title: Tools

docs.title: Make Certificate Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Make certificate dialog, which issues a certificate from a certificate signing request (CSR) and a certificate profile. Open it from Tools > Make Certificate (Shift+F8). A database connection is required.

docs.title: Issue a certificate
docs.text:
1. Select a CSR from the database, or check Use CSR File and click Find to load a CSR file.
  2. Select a certificate profile and review its settings with View if needed.
  3. Confirm or edit the Subject DN. Use Make DN to compose a distinguished name.
  4. Choose whether to issue a self-signed certificate or select the CA certificate that will issue it.
  5. In Pro, optionally enter user information to register along with the certificate.
  6. Click OK to issue and save the certificate. Click Cancel to exit without issuing.

The CSR, certificate profile, and (for CA-signed issuance) issuer certificate are required. For file-based CSR input, Save to Request optionally stores the imported CSR in the database as part of issuance. CertMan checks the CSR signature before issuing. On success, the certificate is saved and the relevant certificate tree/list is refreshed.

docs.title: CSR selection
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose Use CSR File Use a CSR file instead of a CSR record already in the database. This disables the database CSR selector. CSR file path / Find Choose a BER/DER CSR file. The dialog reads the CSR and displays its subject DN when available. Save to Request When using a CSR file, also save that CSR in the database's Request list. Request Name / Num Read-only name and record number of the selected database CSR. Select Opens the CA Manager to select a stored CSR. The associated key-pair description is shown below.

Self-signing is not available when Use CSR File is selected. A stored request's CSR signature must verify successfully before certificate issuance continues.

docs.title: Certificate profile and subject
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose Profile name / Num Read-only name and record number of the selected certificate profile. Select Choose a certificate profile from the Profile Manager. View Inspect the selected profile. Set to default Remember this certificate profile for the next use of the dialog. Subject DN Subject distinguished name to place in the issued certificate. A profile using the CSR DN template takes the request's subject DN. Make DN Opens the DN editor with the current value.

The selected profile supplies certificate version, signature hash, validity period, and extensions. Template placeholders in the subject DN and applicable extension values can be replaced using the Pro User Information fields.

docs.title: Self-signing and CA issuer
docs.text:
• SelfSign issues a self-signed certificate using the key associated with the selected stored CSR. It cannot be used with an external CSR file.
  • For CA-signed issuance, select a CA certificate using Select in the issuer section. The issuer name, record number, and associated key-pair description are displayed.
  • Set to default beside the issuer controls remembers the selected issuer (or the self-sign option) for future use.
  • If the selected CA certificate is expired or revoked, CertMan asks whether to continue.

The CA certificate's associated private key signs the new certificate. The application can use locally stored keys and configured PKCS#11 or KMIP keys.

docs.title: User Information (Pro)
docs.text: The User Information group is shown in Pro. UserName, SSN, and Email are optional. If a UserName is provided, CertMan stores a user record with the issued certificate. These values can also fill user-related placeholders in the certificate subject DN and applicable extensions.

docs.title: Important checks
docs.text:
• The CSR signature must verify.
  • If the CSR public-key algorithm differs from the signing key algorithm, CertMan asks whether to continue.
  • SM2 signing uses the SM3 hash. If the selected profile uses another hash, CertMan may ask whether to change it; an incompatible SM3 selection for other key algorithms is rejected.
  • If the CA certificate is expired or revoked, issuance requires confirmation.

docs.title: Make Certificate Profile Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Make cert profile dialog. Open it from Tools > Make Cert Profile. A database connection is required. The dialog creates reusable certificate profiles; existing profiles can also be edited, copied, or viewed from the Profile Manager.

docs.title: Create a profile
docs.text:
1. On the Base tab, enter a Profile Name.
  2. Choose whether the profile is for a certificate or for CSR Extensions.
  3. For a certificate profile, configure the version, signature hash, validity period, subject DN template, and extension usage.
  4. Use the Extend1 through Extend4 tabs to configure the extensions needed by certificates or CSRs. Each extension has its own controls; select Critical when that extension should be marked critical.
  5. Click OK to save the profile. Click Close to exit without saving.

The profile name is required. For certificate profiles, a subject DN template is also required unless Use CSR DN is selected. On success, CertMan saves the profile and its configured extensions, refreshes the Certificate Profile list, and displays Certificate profile created.

docs.title: Base tab
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose Profile Name Required name for the profile. Version Certificate version. This control is disabled for a profile marked For CSR Extensions. Signature Hash Default signature digest used by the profile where applicable. Disabled for CSR extension profiles. For CSR Extensions Creates a profile intended for CSR extensions. Certificate-specific controls such as version, validity, subject DN, and extension usage are disabled. Valid Period For certificate profiles, choose either a relative duration or explicit dates. Use Days When selected, specify a duration and unit (Day, Month, or Year). New profiles default to 365 days. NotBefore / NotAfter When Use Days is cleared, set explicit start and end date/time values. Subject DN Template Subject name template used for certificates. Click Make DN to compose a DN. Use CSR DN Use the subject DN from the certificate request. When selected, the DN template field is disabled. Extension Usage Choose where extensions are used: certificate only, CSR only, or both with an order preference. Extensions Add custom extensions by entering an OID and hexadecimal value. Use Critical to mark the custom extension critical; Add inserts it into the table and Clear removes table entries.

For a new certificate profile, CertMan defaults to V3, the configured default hash, Use CSR DN, and a 365-day validity period. The extension usage default is The Certificate Extension Only.

docs.title: Extension tabs
docs.text:
The four extension tabs group the supported X.509 extensions. Enter the required values in an extension's controls, then use Add to add table-based values. Clear removes table entries where available. Criticality is configured separately for each extension group.

Tab Extension groups Extend1 Key Usage, Certificate Policies, Subject Key Identifier (SKI), and Authority Key Identifier (AKI). Extend2 Extended Key Usage (EKU), CRL Distribution Points (CRLDP), and Authority Information Access (AIA). Extend3 Basic Constraints, Subject Alternative Name (SAN), and Issuer Alternative Name (IAN). Extend4 Policy Constraints, Policy Mappings, and Name Constraints.

Common value types include usage selections, OIDs, URIs, and typed alternative names. Some groups provide additional fields such as CA/path length, policy counters, or name-constraint distances. Configure only the extensions required by your certificate or request policy.

docs.title: Edit, copy, and view
docs.text:
• Edit loads the saved profile and its extensions. The profile type cannot be changed while editing.
  • Copy loads an existing profile's settings with _Copy appended to its name, allowing you to save a separate profile.
  • View opens the profile in read-only mode.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Certificate and CSR extension profiles share the extension tabs, but the CSR profile type disables certificate-specific base settings.
  • Explicit validity dates are checked to ensure the NotBefore value is not too early. Choose appropriate validity values for your certificate policy.
  • Profile extension contents are stored with the profile in the connected database.

docs.title: Make CRL Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Make CRL dialog, which creates a Certificate Revocation List (CRL) for a selected CA certificate. Open it from Tools > Make CRL (Shift+F9). A database connection is required.

docs.title: Generate a CRL
docs.text:
1. Select a CA certificate with Select. CertMan displays the CA name, record number, and associated key-pair description.
  2. Select a CRL profile. Use View to review it if needed.
  3. Choose a CRLDP value. The list is populated from the selected CA certificate and can also be edited.
  4. Review the Revoked List. It shows revocations for the selected CA and CRL distribution point.
  5. Click OK to generate and save the CRL. Click Cancel to close without generating it.

The CA certificate and CRL profile are required. If the CA certificate is expired or revoked, CertMan asks whether to continue. On success, the generated CRL is saved in the database and the CRL list for the selected CA is refreshed.

docs.title: CA certificate
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose CA Name / Num Read-only subject name and record number of the selected issuer certificate. Select Opens the CA Manager to choose a CA certificate. Key pair description Read-only description of the private key associated with the CA certificate. The associated key signs the CRL.

The selected certificate determines the issuer and the revocation records considered for the CRL. If the certificate is expired or revoked, generation requires confirmation.

docs.title: CRL profile
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose Profile name / Num Read-only name and record number of the selected CRL profile. Select Opens the Profile Manager to choose a CRL profile. View Opens the selected CRL profile for review. Set to default Remember the selected CRL profile for the next use of the dialog. A previously saved default is selected automatically.

The profile provides the CRL version, signature hash, update period, and extensions. If the issuer key is SM2, CertMan requires SM3 or asks whether to change the profile hash to SM3. SM3 is rejected for unsupported issuer key algorithms.

docs.title: Revocation list and CRLDP
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose CRLDP Distribution point filter for revoked certificates included in this CRL. The dropdown is populated from the issuer certificate's CRL distribution points and is editable. Revoked List Read-only list of revoked certificates matching the selected CA and CRLDP, with Serial, Reason, and Date columns.

Changing the CA certificate or CRLDP refreshes the revoked list. The resulting CRL uses the chosen CRLDP value and includes the matching revocation entries.

docs.title: After generation
docs.text: CertMan creates and parses the CRL, stores its issuer, update times, signature algorithm, CRLDP, and encoded data in the database, then refreshes the selected CA's CRL list. The application displays CRL has been generated. A profile marked Auto (Use Sequence) for the CRL Number extension receives the next database sequence value.

docs.title: Related implementation
docs.text: This guide is based on images/make_crl_dlg.png, src/CertMan/make_crl_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/make_crl_dlg.h, src/CertMan/make_crl_dlg.cpp, and the Tools > Make CRL action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: Make CRL Profile Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Make CRL policy dialog, which creates reusable Certificate Revocation List (CRL) profiles. Open it from Tools > Make CRL Profile (Shift+F7). A database connection is required. Existing profiles can also be edited, copied, or viewed from the Profile Manager.

docs.title: Create a CRL profile
docs.text:
1. On the Base tab, enter a CRL Profile Name.
  2. Select the CRL Version and Signature Hash.
  3. Set the CRL update period. Keep Use From Now selected to use a relative period, or clear it to specify explicit update dates.
  4. Open the Extend tab and enable the extension groups you need. Configure each extension's options and criticality.
  5. Click OK to save the profile. Click Close to leave without saving.

The profile name is required. On success, CertMan stores the profile and its extension settings in the connected database, refreshes the CRL Profile list, and displays CRL profile created.

docs.title: Base tab
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose CRL Profile Name Required name for this profile. Version CRL version, either V1 or V2. The default for a new profile is V2. Signature Hash Selects the digest used for the CRL signature. New profiles default to the application's configured hash. CRL Period Controls the This Update and Next Update values. Use From Now When selected, set Valid Period to a number of days, months, or years from the current time. New profiles default to 10 days. This Update / Next Update When Use From Now is cleared, enter explicit date and time values.

The unit dropdown offers Day, Month, and Year. The adjacent label changes to match the selected unit.

docs.title: Extend tab
docs.text:
Each extension group is checkable. Enable the group to include that extension in CRLs created from this profile. Use its Critical checkbox to mark the extension critical where applicable.

Extension Controls and behavior CRL Number Choose Auto (Use Sequence) to use the application sequence, or clear it and enter a fixed value in hexadecimal. The automatic sequence option is selected by default. Authority Key Identifier Add issuer certificate information by selecting Certificate Issuer and/or Certificate Serial. Issuing Distribution Point Select the distribution point type (the UI currently provides URI), enter its value, then click Add. Duplicate values are rejected. Clear removes the listed values. Issuer Alternative Name Choose a value type (URI, email, or DNS), enter a value, and click Add. Duplicate values are rejected. Clear removes the listed values. Extensions Add a custom extension by entering its OID and hexadecimal Value, choosing Critical if needed, and clicking Add. An OID can be added only once. Clear removes all listed custom extensions.

For the table-based Issuing Distribution Point, Issuer Alternative Name, and custom extension entries, you can also select a row and use its context menu to delete that row.

docs.title: Edit, copy, and view
docs.text:
• Edit loads the saved profile and its extension settings. Saving replaces the profile's stored extension list with the current configuration.
  • Copy loads an existing profile's settings and appends _Copy to the name so it can be saved as a separate profile.
  • View opens the profile in read-only mode; the OK button is hidden.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The explicit This Update value is checked to ensure it is not too early. Choose update times and intervals that match your CRL publication policy.
  • Custom extension values are entered as hexadecimal data. The form requires both an OID and a value.
  • Profile settings are saved to the currently connected database.

docs.text: This guide is based on images/make_crl_profile_dlg.png, src/CertMan/make_crl_profile_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/make_crl_profile_dlg.h, src/CertMan/make_crl_profile_dlg.cpp, and the Tools > Make CRL Profile action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: Make Request Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Make request dialog used to create a certificate signing request (CSR). Open it from Tools > Make Request (Shift+F2). A database connection is required.

docs.title: Create a CSR
docs.text:
1. Enter a Name for the request.
  2. Enter the subject DN (Distinguished Name), or click Make DN to compose it with the DN editor.
  3. Optionally enter ChallengePass and UnstructuredName values.
  4. Choose how to provide the signing key:
  5. Keep Generate Key Pair unchecked and use Key Select to choose an existing key pair.
  6. Check Generate Key Pair to create a new key pair in this dialog, then use Key Generate to set its name, algorithm, and parameters.
  7. Optionally check Use Extension and select a CSR profile. Use View to inspect the selected profile.
  8. Choose the Signature Hash when the selected key algorithm supports a separate hash.
  9. Click OK to create and save the CSR. Click Cancel to close without submitting it.

The request name and DN are required. If extensions are enabled, a CSR profile must be selected. If using an existing key, select a key pair first. On success, CertMan saves the request, marks the associated key pair as used, refreshes the Request list, and displays CSR created.

docs.title: Request information
docs.text: Field or control Purpose Name Required name for the CSR record. DN Required subject distinguished name encoded in the request. Make DN Opens the DN editor, retaining the current DN as its starting value. ChallengePass Optional challenge password attribute. UnstructuredName Optional unstructured name attribute. Signature Hash Selects the digest used for the CSR signature when applicable. The initial value comes from the application's default hash setting.

docs.title: Select an existing key pair
docs.text:
When Generate Key Pair is unchecked, the Key Select tab is used:

Field or control Purpose Key Name Read-only name of the selected key pair. Num Read-only database record number for the key pair. Select Opens the CA Manager selection dialog. Choose a key pair and confirm. Key pair description Read-only description of the selected key pair.

The key's algorithm and parameters are taken from the selected database record. For PKCS#11 or KMIP keys, the corresponding configured provider is used to create the CSR signature.

docs.title: Generate a new key pair
docs.text:
Check Generate Key Pair to switch to the Key Generate tab. The existing-key tab becomes unavailable until the checkbox is cleared.

Field or control Purpose Key Name Required database name for the newly generated key pair. CertMan may suggest the request name followed by _keyPair. Mechanism Select RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, or SM2. The PQC row contains ML-DSA and SLH-DSA. Public Exponent RSA public exponent, initially 65537; disabled for algorithms that do not use it. Key Length / parameter dropdown Select the mechanism-specific key size, curve, or parameter set. Defaults to RSA 2048 unless changed by a saved key-generation preference. To PKCS#11 Generate the key through a configured PKCS#11 token/HSM when supported and available. To KMIP Generate through KMIP. This control is shown in Pro and depends on the configured KMIP provider.

The available key parameters follow the choices in the New keypair dialog: RSA sizes 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, and 8192; DSA sizes 1024, 2048, and 3072; supported named curves for ECDSA; Ed25519/Ed448; SM2; ML-DSA-44/65/87; and the SLH-DSA SHA2/SHAKE parameter sets. Exact availability can depend on the selected storage provider and edition.

docs.title: CSR profile and extensions
docs.text:
• Use Extension enables the CSR profile controls.
  • CSR Profile displays the selected profile name and record number. Click Select to choose a profile; click View to inspect it.
  • The Set to default checkbox beside the extension controls saves the extension/profile selection for later use. The last selection is restored when the dialog is opened again.
  • When a profile includes Subject Key Identifier or Authority Key Identifier extensions, CertMan derives the key identifier from the public key while building the request.

docs.title: Signature hash behavior
docs.text: The hash dropdown is disabled for EdDSA, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA, whose signature algorithms determine the digest behavior. Selecting SM2 sets the hash to SM3. When an existing key pair is selected, the dialog adjusts hash availability based on that key.

docs.title: Edition and configuration notes
docs.text:
• In the unlicensed version, RSA is selected and the other mechanism choices are disabled.
  • To PKCS#11 is disabled when the PKCS#11 context is unavailable. PKCS#11 use also requires valid settings and an accessible session.
  • To KMIP is hidden outside Pro. It requires KMIP configuration.
  • Some algorithm/storage combinations are restricted by the dialog. For example, PKCS#11 selection disables SM2 and the PQC mechanisms in the key-generation controls.
  • For internally stored keys, CertMan uses its private-key password feature when that feature is enabled.

docs.title: New Key Pair Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the New keypair dialog in CertMan. The dialog is opened from Tools > New keypair (shortcut: Shift+F1). A database must be connected before you can open it.

docs.title: Create a key pair
docs.text:
1. Enter a unique, recognizable value in Name. The name is required.
  2. Select a Mechanism. Choose one of the standard algorithms, or a post-quantum algorithm in the PQC row.
  3. Select the parameter or key length from the dropdown. The available choices depend on the selected mechanism.
  4. For RSA, review or change Exponent. It defaults to 65537. This field is disabled for algorithms that do not use an RSA exponent.
  5. Optionally select a key storage destination, if available and configured.
  6. Select Set to default if you want this algorithm and parameter selection to be preselected the next time the dialog opens.
  7. Click OK to generate and save the key pair. Click Close to leave without generating it.

After successful generation, CertMan stores the key pair in the connected database, refreshes the KeyPair list, and reports Key pair generated. If generation fails, the dialog displays an error.

docs.title: Fields and options
docs.text: Control Purpose Name Database name for the key pair. It cannot be empty. Mechanism Select RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, or SM2. PQC Select ML-DSA or SLH-DSA, the post-quantum algorithm choices. Key Length / parameter dropdown Choose the algorithm-specific size, curve, or parameter set. The label changes to match the selected algorithm. Exponent RSA public exponent; the initial value is 65537. To PKCS#11 Generate using a configured PKCS#11 token or HSM. This option is unavailable if the PKCS#11 provider is not loaded. To KMIP Generate through KMIP. This option is shown in Pro and requires suitable KMIP configuration. Set to default Save the selected algorithm, parameter, and HSM choice as the dialog's next default. OK Generate and save the key pair. Close Close the dialog without submitting the form.

docs.title: Algorithm parameters
docs.text:
The parameter dropdown is populated for the selected mechanism:

Mechanism Choices provided by the application RSA Key sizes: 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, or 8192 bits. ECDSA Named elliptic curves, including prime256v1, secp256k1, secp384r1, and secp521r1. The full list is available in the dropdown. DSA Key sizes: 1024, 2048, or 3072 bits. EdDSA Ed25519 or Ed448. SM2 SM2 parameter. ML-DSA ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, or ML-DSA-87. SLH-DSA SHA2 or SHAKE parameter sets at 128-, 192-, or 256-bit security levels, with s and f variants.

docs.title: Availability and storage notes
docs.text:
• The unlicensed version selects RSA and disables the other mechanism choices.
  • The To PKCS#11 option is enabled only when the PKCS#11 context is available. PKCS#11 settings and a usable token/session are also required when generating.
  • To KMIP appears in Pro. KMIP supports the mechanisms implemented by the application; some mechanism choices are disabled while KMIP is selected.
  • ML-DSA and SLH-DSA use the application's software key generation path even if PKCS#11 is selected; they are not generated as PKCS#11 keys by this dialog implementation.
  • Key generation requires a connected database. Internal private keys are encrypted when CertMan's private-key password feature is enabled.

docs.title: OCSP Service Manual
docs.text: The OCSP Service dialog runs an Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responder. Configure its CA certificate, OCSP signing certificate, and listener settings before starting it.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose Service > OCSP Service from the main window.

docs.title: Configure the service
docs.text:
1. Enter the listener Port.
  2. In CA certificate and private key, click Select to choose the CA certificate used by the responder. Use View to inspect it.
  3. In OCSP Server Certificate and Private Key, click Select to choose the certificate and associated private key used to sign OCSP responses. Use View to inspect it.
  4. Optionally check Need Sign to enable the responder's response-signing option.
  5. To enable encrypted transport, check TLS. Then select the certificate and private key in TLS Certificate and Private Key. Use View to inspect the selected TLS certificate.
  6. Optionally check Set to default to save the current configuration for the next time the dialog opens.
  7. Click Start. The button turns green when the server starts, and runtime messages appear in the log.

The CA certificate and OCSP signing certificate/private key must be available. When TLS is enabled, its certificate and private key must also be available. The application reports errors for missing ports, unavailable certificate or key records, unsupported PKCS#11 TLS certificates, or a listener that fails to start.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Stop stops the OCSP responder.
  • Log Clear clears the displayed log.
  • Close closes the dialog.
  • Set to default saves the port, TLS and Need Sign options, and selected CA, OCSP, and TLS certificate numbers. If unchecked when the service starts, the saved default is cleared.

docs.title: Profile Manager Manual
docs.text: The Profile Manager displays the certificate, CSR, and CRL profiles saved in the current CertMan database. In management mode, you can inspect a profile or delete it. Create or modify profiles through the corresponding profile creation tools.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose Tools > Profile Manager from the main window. The manager opens as a modeless window, so you can return to the main window while it remains open.

docs.title: Certificate Profile tab
docs.text:
The Certificate Profile tab lists certificate and CSR profiles. Use the selector at the upper right to switch between Certificate and CSR profiles. The table shows:

  • Num: profile record number.
  • NotBefore and NotAfter: the configured validity period.
  • Name: profile name.

Select a row, then click View to open the profile details. You can also double-click a row or right-click the table and choose View. To remove the selected profile, click Delete or use the right-click Delete command, then confirm the prompt. The list refreshes after a successful deletion.

docs.title: CRL Profile tab
docs.text: The CRL Profile tab lists saved CRL profiles. The table shows the profile number, ThisUpdate, NextUpdate, and Name. Select a row and click View to inspect its details; double-clicking or using the right-click View command also opens the profile. To delete a profile, click Delete or choose it from the right-click menu and confirm.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The tables do not allow direct editing. View opens a read-only profile details window.
  • Deletion requires confirmation and removes the selected profile record from the current database.
  • If no row is selected, the manager displays a warning when you request View or Delete.
  • Click Close to close the manager.

docs.title: Publish to LDAP Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Publish to ldap dialog. Open it from Data > Publish to LDAP (Ctrl+Alt+L) for a selected certificate or CRL. The command requires a licensed version and an open database.

docs.title: Publish an object
docs.text:
1. Enter the LDAP Host, Port, Bind DN, and Password.
  2. Choose Data Type (Certificate or CRL).
  3. Choose an LDAP Attribute appropriate to the data type.
  4. Review or edit Publish DN. It is initially derived from the certificate subject or, for a CRL, its LDAP distribution point when available.
  5. Optionally keep Set to default selected to remember the host, port, and Bind DN.
  6. Click OK to bind to the LDAP server, create any missing parent entries, and publish the object. Click Cancel to exit.

Host, Bind DN, password, and Publish DN are required. Port defaults to 389 when blank. CertMan displays a success message after publishing.

docs.title: Fields and choices
docs.text:
Field Purpose Set to default Save the host, port, and Bind DN in application settings for future use. The password is not included in these saved defaults. Host LDAP server hostname or IP address. Defaults to localhost when no saved host exists. Port LDAP server port; defaults to 389. Bind DN Distinguished name used to authenticate to LDAP. Password Password for the Bind DN; displayed as masked text. Source information Read-only summary of the selected certificate or CRL. Data Type Select Certificate or CRL. Attribute Certificate: caCertificate, signCertificate, or userCertificate. CRL: certificateRevocationList or authorityRevocationList. Publish DN LDAP distinguished name where the object is published.

For a certificate, the initial Publish DN is derived from its subject DN. For a CRL, an LDAP CRLDP value is used as the initial value when present. You can edit the DN before publishing.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The LDAP bind and publish operation modifies the target directory. Confirm that the selected attribute and DN match the directory schema and intended destination.
  • The dialog creates missing parent entries before publishing the selected certificate or CRL.
  • Saved defaults include connection host, port, and Bind DN, but do not store the password or Publish DN.

docs.text: This guide is based on images/pub_ldap_dlg.png, src/CertMan/pub_ldap_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/pub_ldap_dlg.h, src/CertMan/pub_ldap_dlg.cpp, and the Data > Publish to LDAP action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: Revoke Certificate Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Revoke certificate dialog. Select a certificate in the main window and choose Revoke Certificate from the context menu or Tools > Revoke Certificate (Shift+F10). A database connection is required.

docs.title: Revoke a certificate
docs.text:
1. Confirm the read-only Subject DN and Serial shown for the selected certificate.
  2. Set the DateTime of revocation. It defaults to the current date and time.
  3. Choose a Reason. The default is unspecified.
  4. Click OK to record the revocation, or Cancel to leave without saving.

When confirmed, CertMan adds a revocation record for the selected certificate, changes its status to revoked, and refreshes the issuer's Revoked List. The reason and date are used when a CRL is generated.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Purpose Subject DN Read-only subject distinguished name of the selected certificate. Serial Read-only field labeled Serial. The current dialog populates it with the certificate's database record number; the saved revocation record uses the certificate's actual serial number. DateTime Revocation date and time. Initially set to the current local date and time. Reason Revocation reason recorded for the certificate. OK Save the revocation and update the certificate status. Cancel Close without recording a revocation.

Available reasons include unspecified, keyCompromise, CACompromise, affiliationChanged, superseded, cessationOfOperation, certificateHold, removeFromCRL, holdInstruction, keyTime, and CAKeyTime.

docs.title: Restrictions
docs.text:
• Select a certificate row before opening the command. The command is unavailable when the current list is not a certificate list.
  • A self-signed Root CA certificate cannot be revoked through this command.
  • For a CA certificate that is not a self-signed Root CA, revoke carefully: newly generated CRLs for that issuer can publish the revocation.

docs.text: This guide is based on images/revoke_cert_dlg.png, src/CertMan/revoke_cert_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/revoke_cert_dlg.h, src/CertMan/revoke_cert_dlg.cpp, and the Revoke Certificate action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: Settings Manual
docs.text: The Settings dialog contains general application preferences and configuration for connected services. Settings are organized into tabs. Some service settings are available only in the licensed or PRO editions.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose Settings from the main window.

docs.title: Base tab
docs.text:
Use Base to configure common behavior and defaults:

  • Check for updates automatically enables automatic update checks when supported by the build.
  • LDAP Information sets the LDAP host, port, and BaseDN used by LDAP operations.
  • ListCount controls the number of rows shown in list views.
  • Server status check controls the application's server-status checking behavior.
  • Use log tab at startup opens the log tab on startup.
  • Default Hash sets the default hash algorithm, and Default ECCParam sets the default elliptic-curve parameter where available.
  • Font Family selects the application font.
  • PKCS8 PKCS12 encryption method chooses the encryption method used for these private-key/container formats.
  • Save Remote Information controls whether remote connection information is saved.

docs.title: Advanced tab
docs.text:
• Language changes the application language. A restart is required for the change to take effect.
  • Show private key value controls whether private-key values are displayed in the interface.
  • Use PKCS11 enables PKCS#11 integration. Set the Library Path, Slot Index, and PIN as needed. Use Find to locate the PKCS#11 library. The slot index identifies the slot position to use.
  • Use fixed hex area / Characters adjusts the fixed-width hexadecimal display area.

docs.title: Service tabs
docs.text:
The other tabs configure connection information for external services. Enable each service's information group before using its settings.

  • KMIP: host, port, CA certificate, client certificate, private key, username, and password. Use Find beside certificate and key paths to browse for files.
  • OCSP: responder URI and server certificate. Attach Signature enables the optional signature attachment and allows signer certificate and private-key paths to be set.
  • CMP: server URI, root CA certificate, and CA certificate.
  • REG: registration server URI, administrator name, and password.
  • TSP: timestamp server URI and server certificate.
  • SCEP: SCEP URI. SSL Mutual Auth enables mutual TLS authentication and its client certificate and private-key paths.

Use the Find buttons to select the associated files. These tabs and some Base-tab options may be restricted by the installed edition.

docs.title: Save or discard changes
docs.text:
• Click OK to save the settings and close the dialog. If the language changed, the application asks whether to restart now.
  • Click Cancel to close without applying the edits from this dialog.
  • Click Restore defaults to clear saved settings and return to defaults. Confirm the prompt; the application then offers to restart to apply them.

docs.title: Set Password Dialog Guide
docs.text:
This guide describes the SetPassDlg password prompt used when creating a new CertMan database. It is not the dialog opened by Data > Set Passwd: that menu action opens the private-key encryption progress window.

Image note: The supplied set_pass_dlg.png shows a Progress Status Window with Encrypt Private, which does not match the SetPassDlg layout in src/CertMan/set_pass_dlg.ui. The guide below documents the source dialog; the image is included as provided and should be replaced with a screenshot of the password prompt when one is available.

docs.title: When this dialog appears
docs.text: The main-window File > New command (Ctrl+N) opens this dialog with the heading Set private key password before prompting for a new database location. The dialog collects the password preference; when the database is created, CertMan saves the password verifier and enables private-key encryption only if the application is licensed and Use password is selected.

docs.title: Set a password
docs.text:
1. Leave Use password selected to encrypt internal private keys saved in the new database.
  2. Enter a value in Password and enter it again in Password Confirm.
  3. Click OK to accept. The values must match.
  4. To create the database without this private-key password protection, clear Use password and click OK. The warning text changes to indicate the unsafe setting.
  5. Click Cancel to cancel the database creation flow.

When Use password is cleared, the password fields are disabled and no password is required. The main window does not store the password configuration in an unlicensed database.

docs.title: Fields and controls
docs.text:
Field or control Purpose Heading Set by the calling workflow; for new database creation it reads Set private key password. Use password Enable or disable password protection. Checked by default. Some callers can require it and hide the checkbox. Description Explains that the password encrypts private keys, or warns that the setting is unsafe when password use is disabled. Password New password. Input is masked. Password Confirm Re-enter the password. Input is masked and must match. OK Accept the choice after validation. Cancel Reject the dialog and return to the caller.

The dialog rejects an empty password, an empty confirmation, or a mismatch when Use password is checked. It does not itself encrypt keys; the caller saves the password verifier and subsequent key operations use the configured password.

docs.title: Important distinction
docs.text: The separate Data > Set Passwd (Ctrl+Alt+P) action requires an open, licensed database with unencrypted private keys. It starts a progress operation to encrypt internal private keys; it does not open SetPassDlg. Data > Change Passwd similarly uses a progress operation when keys are already encrypted.

docs.text: This guide is based on images/set_pass_dlg.png, src/CertMan/set_pass_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/set_pass_dlg.h, src/CertMan/set_pass_dlg.cpp, and the File > New call site in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: TSP Service Manual
docs.text: The TSP Service dialog runs a Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP) server using a selected TSP signing certificate and private key. You can optionally secure its listener with TLS.

docs.title: Open the dialog
docs.text: Choose Service > TSP Service from the main window.

docs.title: Configure the service
docs.text:
1. Enter the listener Port.
  2. In TSP Server Certificate and Private Key, click Select and choose the certificate used to sign timestamp responses. The selected certificate number and name appear in the fields; use View to inspect it.
  3. To enable encrypted transport, check TLS. The TLS Server Certificate and Private Key section becomes available. Click its Select button to choose the TLS server certificate and associated private key. Use View to inspect the selected certificate.
  4. Optionally check Set to default to save these settings for the next time the dialog opens.
  5. Click Start. A successful start is indicated by the Start button turning green, and server messages appear in the log.

The TSP signing certificate is required. When TLS is enabled, a TLS certificate and private key are also required. The application reports an error if the port is empty, a selected record or key cannot be loaded, or the server cannot start. TLS certificates backed by PKCS#11 are not supported by this dialog.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Stop stops the running TSP server.
  • Log Clear clears the messages displayed in the log.
  • Close closes the dialog.
  • Set to default stores the listener port, TLS setting, and selected certificate numbers as the next-use defaults. Leaving it unchecked clears the saved default when the service starts.

docs.title: User Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains CertMan's Register a user dialog. Open it from Tools > Register User. A database connection is required. The same dialog can also be opened for an existing user to modify that record.

docs.title: Register or update a user in CertMan
docs.text:
1. Enter the user's Name, SSN, and Email. These three fields are required.
  2. Choose a Status. New dialogs default to Register.
  3. Optionally enter a RefNum and AuthCode, or use the buttons beside those fields to generate values.
  4. Click OK to save the record to the currently connected database. Click Cancel to close without saving.

After saving, CertMan refreshes the User list. If the dialog was opened for an existing user, it updates that record; otherwise, it adds a new user record.

docs.title: Fields and controls
docs.text: Field or control Purpose Name Required user name. SSN Required SSN value used by the application as the user's identifier. Email Required email address. Status User status. The available values are Invalid, Register, Issue, and Stop. New records default to Register. RefNum Optional reference number. Click the RefNum button to fill the next sequence number based on the latest user record in the database. AuthCode Optional authorization code. Click AuthCode to generate a random code and populate the field. RegServer In Pro, submit the user's name, SSN, and email to the configured registration server. OK Save the user record to the local CertMan database, or update the loaded record. Cancel Close without saving changes to the local database.

docs.title: Register with the registration server
docs.text: The RegServer button is available in Pro. It sends the current Name, SSN, and Email to the configured REG server after signing in. A successful response displays a confirmation and refreshes the User list. This is a separate action from clicking OK, which saves the local database record. REG server settings and a successful login are required.

docs.title: Editing an existing user
docs.text: When opened for an existing record, the dialog title changes to Modify a user and the stored name, SSN, email, authorization code, and reference number are loaded. Change the desired values and click OK to update the record. The status selector is initialized to Register when the dialog is shown; review it before saving an edit.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The dialog validates that Name, SSN, and Email are not empty. It does not perform additional format validation in this form.
  • The RefNum and AuthCode fields are optional for local saving.
  • The RegServer button is hidden outside the Pro edition.

docs.title: Related implementation
docs.text: This guide is based on images/user_dlg.png, src/CertMan/user_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/user_dlg.h, src/CertMan/user_dlg.cpp, and the Register User action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.
